name: lnk_jumplist
description: Read shell links and Jump Lists as one set of rows, each with where its structure sits in the file, what it decodes to, and whether it holds together. An adapter, not a new decoder: a link is decoded by this pack's lnk_parse, a DestList by the layouts of this pack's jumplist, a link is read again by liblnk's `lnkinfo` as an independent reader, and a DestList is read again by Eric Zimmerman's `JLECmd` (through dotnet) where it is installed; what this tool adds is the part those do not do. It reads the OLE compound file an automaticDestinations-ms is stored in (MS-CFB, standard library only) and says where every stream sits, whether the container is consistent: the header (version, sector size, mini stream cutoff, the counts it gives), the DIFAT (a FAT sector named twice, outside the file or more of them than a file this size can need, a chain that loops or is longer than the file can need), the FAT (each FAT and DIFAT sector marked as such, the counts of the marks), the directory (names of a possible length, object types, a tree that loops, names an entry twice or names one that is not allocated, an allocated entry the tree never reaches, a stream with a child), the mini FAT and the mini stream, and every chain (a loop, a sector outside the file or the FAT, a free or FAT-marked link, a chain longer or shorter than the size it serves, and a sector or mini sector that two chains hold: the second chain is followed no further, its row says where it stops), which DestList entry names which stream, and which entries have no stream and which streams no entry. A DestList entry that names a stream that is not a shell link, two entries that name one stream, and a container that holds streams and no DestList are container problems (a container with no stream at all, which is what Windows leaves for an empty jump list, is not); a stream the DestList has no entry for is a finding in its row. Every problem is listed once in the container row with how many more of its kind there were; a stream's own problems are in its row, and a stream's extents beyond the first 32 are counted in the row (`extents_not_shown`) and follow its chain from the start sector. A customDestinations-ms has no container: its link structures are carved by the 20-byte header, each marked carved, and the container is not parsed. Inputs: a .lnk, an automaticDestinations-ms, a customDestinations-ms, or a directory of them (walked, links not followed; a file of another kind is counted, named and not read). A file named as `path` is classified by its first bytes; one in a directory by its name and first bytes. Rows (row: file, container, stream, destlist_entry, link): every offset inside a link's record is from the start of that link structure, and `file_offset` and `extents` say where the structure sits in the file. A link row has the header FILETIMEs raw (decimal) beside ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits, the structured target (local path with VolumeID: drive type, serial as eight hex digits, label; or a network target with share, device and provider), the string fields (arguments_first_token is a program, a script or a known switch name, otherwise null with arguments_first_token_withheld), the tracker blocks (the first 16; tracker_count says how many, and a link with more than 16 is an incomplete row, so the status is partial), and `integrity`: structure_complete, lnk_parse's problems, and what lnkinfo says (time, size, volume, target and label compared field by field, or why it was not run). The rows are JSON Lines: `limit` rows are shown inline and the whole set is in the file the answer names (`rows_file`). status is complete only when no row is incomplete, no container problem is named, lnkinfo and JLECmd disagree nowhere, nothing was left unread and the tool's own clock did not run out; the status_basis says which. Not done: a link's target is not resolved or opened, a DestList's access counters are returned raw as lnk_parse/jumplist return them (no access count is claimed), and a customDestinations-ms's categories, pins and tasks are not parsed. A FIFO, socket or device is never opened: it is counted under not_attempted and the status is partial. Bounds: a link file past 64 MiB is named and not parsed, at most 32 MiB of one container stream is read (the rest is named, and the status is partial), at most 20,000 files of a directory are read (max_files), and the tool's own clock (max_seconds) ends the walk with what was read; memory stays bounded because files are read in pieces and each sector is held by one chain at a time, a DestList is read whole up to 64 MiB and at most 50,000 of its entries are kept (the rest is named by where it starts, and the status is partial), and a DestList entry is matched to the streams by name and to the file by bisection with the clock looked at, so the work is linear in the sectors of the file and the entries however many streams name one chain (a DestList of 580,000 entries held whole was 873 MB; a 1 MB file whose DIFAT lists one FAT sector 254,000 times, and a 2 MB file with 400 streams on one 4,000-sector chain, each ran in 0.1 s at about 35 MB resident; a 300 MiB sparse jump list was read at about 32 MB resident). The tool's own clock is looked at while the FAT, the chains, the streams and the DestList entries are read; when it is reached the streams not yet examined have no row, the container row says how many were, and the status is partial. SENSITIVE and withheld by shape: a link's arguments, its UTF-16 string scan, and a path-like field shaped like a secret are handled as lnk_parse handles them: not in the answer. The answer gives arguments_present, arguments_chars and arguments_first_token; the text goes only to lnk-strings.jsonl under $OUT with mode 0600 when write_strings is true, and write_strings is refused unless the tool runs as a job with secret_output: true (nothing is made when it is refused). A secret in a field that does not look like one is printed with the rest. The two sibling tools it loads (lnk_parse and jumplist) carry their own stop handlers; loading them does not replace this tool's: a SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP while lnkinfo or JLECmd runs ends it and what it started, removes the temporary .xcheck files and JLECmd's directory, and answers with this tool's own interrupted document. JLECmd, the second reader of a DestList: for each automaticDestinations-ms whose DestList this tool read (at least one entry, and not cut at the 50,000-entry bound), JLECmd is run once, `JLECmd -f <the file> --csv <a directory of its own under $OUT> --dt "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fffffff" -q`, through dotnet, in this tool's process group, with its output in files in that directory, and the directory is removed afterwards. The CSV it writes is compared with the DestList read field by field: the entry count, and for each entry (joined by its entry number) the path, the access time to 100 nanoseconds, the pin state, and the application id against the file name when the name is one. Each destlist_entry row has `integrity.jlecmd` with `result` agree, disagree or not_run (with the `compared` fields, the `differences` or the `why`), and the destlist row has the file's own: the counts, a difference in the count or in the application id, and an entry only JLECmd lists. A disagreement makes the status partial and names how many jump lists and entries differ; a JLECmd that is absent, exits non-zero, writes no CSV or an unreadable one (a column missing, a time not given to 100 nanoseconds, a pin state that is neither Pinned nor Unpinned), runs out of time or reaches the output cap is not_run with the reason (the receipt's `jlecmd` counts them, `failed` is those that ran and gave nothing), and is never agree. Its bounds: a run is given at most 30 seconds and its limit ends 6 seconds before the tool's own clock does (when fewer than 9 seconds are left it is not started), at most 200 jump lists in one call are given to it (the rest are not_run, said), and no file it writes may pass 32 MiB (the file-size limit the tool sets on JLECmd stops the writer where the host lets it, and a file that reached the cap is not read). An entry whose DestList FILETIME is 0 is compared with JLECmd's 1601-01-01 00:00:00.0000000, and one past year 9999 is listed in the entry's `not_compared` and not counted among its `compared` fields. JLECmd's option names, its CSV columns, the EntryNumber mapping to the DestList entry number and LastModified as the access time come from the pinned build's help strings and metadata, not from a real run of it: a CSV that does not fit is not_run or disagree, never agree. A customDestinations-ms, a lone link, a container without a DestList, a DestList this tool read no entry of and a DestList it read only to its first 50,000 entries are not given to it. What JLECmd prints on standard output and standard error is not kept, and the CSV columns this tool does not compare (its Arguments column among them) are not read into any row. The directory walk is under the same clock (looked at per directory and every 256 entries): when it runs out the answer is partial and says after how many entries; the files the walk passes over are counted (skipped) and the first 5,000 are named in the receipt. `complete` also needs that JLECmd left nothing behind (lnkinfo prints on a pipe and is not held to this): a process it leaves running (in the tool's process group or in a session of its own) is stopped, killed and reaped by the shared process block's settle() before its CSV is read; one found makes the answer `partial`, the second read of that DestList is not made (integrity.jlecmd `not_run`, with the reason) and program_group.left_behind counts it; on a host that is not Linux, or where the kernel refuses PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, the absence of a leftover cannot be proven and a run that read JLECmd's CSV is at most `partial` (program_group.unproven).

path.description: A shell link, a Jump List file, or a directory of them

limit.description: Rows shown inline (default 100, an inline page size); every row is kept, and the whole set is in the file the answer names

max_files.description: Most files read from a directory (default 20000); those past it are counted and the status is partial

write_strings.description: Write the withheld text (arguments, the UTF-16 strings, a secret-shaped field) to lnk-strings.jsonl under $OUT, mode 0600 (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job with secret_output: true; the answer never carries a value

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds, 1 to 110 (default 100); files after it are not read, the answer says so and is partial
